challenge.method: Read all four branches and the definition of attachment. Test competing conversion and copy-semantics cases and separate abstract effect from an implementation sequence. Compare the exact predecessor and its source revision to the revised claim and trigger conditions.
challenge.results: Where the valid reference-semantics case applies without conversion, attachment is to the existing object. Void and copy-semantics cases have separate effects. The claim has Eiffel-specific triggers for Ecma revision and corrections, byte changes, and contrary evidence. Its due date, substantive scope, proposition, and exact citations match the predecessor.

limitations: The result is the normative abstract effect under the stated condition. Internal representation and clone strategies are unverified.

Both unchanged Ecma source revision-1 records retain a suited trigger for publisher correction, material edition change, byte drift, or contrary applicable evidence. They also retain an unrelated BQN draft trigger. Its extra review burden is a source metadata quality issue. It cannot narrow the relevant triggers, extend the due date, change the source scope, or affect the factual dependency.
